'''Ana María Gayoso''' (20 August 1948 – 28 December 2004) was an Argentine marine biologist, a specialist in study of marine phytoplankton,<ref name=":0" /> best known for being the first scientist to describe [[phytoplankton]] in the [[Bahía Blanca]] Estuary,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=Ana Maria |title=Seasonal Succession Patterns of Phytoplankton in the Bahía Blanca Estuary (Argentina) |journal=Botanica Marina |date=1999 |volume=42 |issue=4 |pages=367–375 |doi=10.1515/BOT.1999.042|s2cid=85904295 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=Ana Maria |title=Long-term phytoplankton studies in the Bahía Blanca estuary, Argentina |journal=ICES Journal of Marine Science |date=1998 |volume=55 |issue=4 |page=665-660 |doi=10.1006/jmsc.1998.0375|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Species of the Diatom Genus Thalass">{{cite journal |last1=Ana Maria |first1=Gayoso |title=Species of the Diatom Genus Thalassiosira from a Coastal Zone of the South Atlantic (Argentina) |journal=Botanica Marina |date=1989 |volume=32 |issue=4 |pages=331–337 |doi=10.1515/botm.1989.32.4.331|s2cid=85321083 }}</ref> and to initiate the sustained long-term oceanographic dataset in this ecosystem. She made significant contributions to the understanding of [[harmful algal bloom]]s caused by [[Dinotoxin|toxic dinoflagellate]] species in the Patagonian gulfs,<ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=Ana Maria |title=Occurrence patterns of Alexandrium tamarense (Lebour) Balech populations in the Golfo Nuevo (Patagonia, Argentina), with observations on ventral pore occurrence in natural and cultured cells |journal=Harmful Algae |date=2006 |volume=5 |issue=3 |pages=233–241 |doi=10.1016/j.hal.2004.12.010}}</ref> and was the first scientist to describe high abundances of the [[coccolithophore]] [[Emiliania huxleyi]] in the Argentine Sea,<ref name=":2">{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=Ana Maria |title=Bloom of Emiliania huxleyi (Prymnesiophyceae) in the western South Atlantic Ocean |journal=Journal of Plankton Research |date=1995 |volume=17 |issue=8 |pages=1717–1722 |doi=10.1093/plankt/17.8.1717}}</ref> a key component in the primary productivity along the Patagonian Shelf Break front in the SW South Atlantic. She started the most extensive (1978–present) long-term database of phytoplankton and physico-chemical variables in South America,<ref name=":3">{{cite web |last1=Antares |url=http://www.antares.ws/?p=About.html |website=Antares | title = Antares Website}}</ref> in a fixed monitoring site in the Bahía Blanca Estuary.<ref name="AL2017"/><ref name="G2012"/><ref name="G2010"/> She died on 28 December 2004 in [[Puerto Madryn]].

== Education ==
Gayoso graduated in botany and obtained a PhD<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Gayoso |first1=Ana Maria |title=Tesis de doctorado |url=http://sedici.unlp.edu.ar/handle/10915/5043 |website=SEDICI |year=1981 |access-date=25 January 2022|type=Tesis }}</ref> in Natural Sciences at the Faculty of Natural Sciences and Museum of the [[National University of La Plata]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Museo de la Plata |url=https://www.museo.fcnym.unlp.edu.ar/}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
In 1977, she became a researcher in the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council]], CONICET, Argentina. From 1978 to 1995 she worked at the Argentine Institute of Oceanography (IADO<ref>{{cite web |url=https://iado.conicet.gov.ar/ | title = IADO-CONICET Website}}</ref>) in Bahía Blanca, where she led the Plankton Laboratory. Her scientific career focused on the study of marine phytoplankton<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=Ana Maria |title=Surface hydrography and phytoplankton of the Brazil-Malvinas currents confluence |journal=Journal of Plankton Research |date=1996 |volume=18 |issue=6 |pages=941–951 |doi=10.1093/plankt/18.6.941|doi-access=free }}</ref> in the South Western South Atlantic.

In 1989 she participated in an oceanographic cruise along the Argentine Sea and characterized the phytoplankton of the [[Brazil–Malvinas Confluence]]. In particular, she specialized on the taxonomy and ecology of [[diatom]]s and [[Dinotoxin|toxic dinoflagellates]].

She made significant contributions to the understanding of [[harmful algal bloom]]s caused by [[Dinotoxin|toxic dinoflagellate]] species in the Patagonian gulfs,<ref name=":1" /> and was the first scientist to describe high abundances of the coccolithophore [[Emiliania huxleyi]] in the Argentine Sea,<ref name=":2" /> a key component in the primary productivity along the Patagonian Shelf Break front in the SW South Atlantic. She started the most extensive (1978–present) long-term database of phytoplankton and physico-chemical variables in South America,<ref name=":3" /> in a fixed monitoring site in the Bahía Blanca Estuary.<ref name="AL2017" /><ref name="G2012" /><ref name="G2010" />

She  applied electron microscopy techniques in the identification of marine diatom species in the Argentine Sea, such as the first morphological description of ''Thalassiosira hibernalis'' A.M. Gayoso, 1989,<ref name="Species of the Diatom Genus Thalass"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Thalassiosira hibernalis A.M.Gayoso 1989 |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/species/detail/?tc=accept&tc=accept&species_id=48461 |website=AlgaeBase | series =Algaease Website}}</ref> and the [[ecophysiology]] of the key blooming species ''Thalassiosira curviseriata''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=Ana Maria |title=Effect of irradiance and temperature on the growth rate of Thalassiosira curviseriata Takano (Bacillariophyceae), a bloom diatom in Bahia Blanca estuary (Argentina) |journal=Journal of Plankton Research |date=1999 |volume=21 |issue=6 |pages=1101–1110 |doi=10.1093/plankt/21.6.1101|doi-access=free }}</ref> isolated from the Bahía Blanca Estuary.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://whsrn.org/es/whsrn_sites/estuario-de-la-bahia-blanca/ |website=WHSRN | title =WHSRN Website}}</ref> During her work at IADO, she contributed to technical reports assessing the water quality of large reservoirs which supply cities in the area, contributing to the detection and description of nuisance [[cyanobacteria]] blooms,<ref>{{cite news |title=Harmful Algae News |url=http://hab.ioc-unesco.org/index.php?option=com_oe&task=viewDocumentRecord&docID=2834 |agency=Harmful Algal Bloom Programme |issue=5 |publisher=Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO |date=1993}}</ref> potentially toxic for human health.

Since 1995, she worked at  the National Patagonian Center ([https://cenpat.conicet.gov.ar/ CENPAT-CONICET]) in Puerto Madryn and was co-director of the institute during 1998–2000, where she made important contributions to the understanding of harmful algal blooms (HABs) or "red tides" prevalent in the Patagonian gulfs since the first HABs event registered in 1981,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Carreto |first1=José |title=Los fenómenos de marea roja y toxicidad de moluscos bivalvos en el Mar Argentino |date=1981 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277129064}}</ref> with particular interest in the toxic dinoflagellates [[Alexandrium (dinoflagellate)|Alexandrium]] spp.<ref name="Observations on Alexandrium tamaren">{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=Ana Maria |title=Observations on Alexandrium tamarense (Lebour) Balech and Other Dinoflagellate Populations in Golfo Nuevo, Patagonia (Argentina) |journal=Journal of Plankton Research |date=2001 |volume=23 |issue=5 |pages=463–468 |doi=10.1093/plankt/23.5.463|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":1"/>

She worked with [[Theodore Smayda]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.9thushab.com/in-memoriam | title = Memorandum of Theodore Smayda}}</ref> at the [[University of Rhode Island]] on diatoms<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/species/detail/?tc=accept&species_id=56302 |website=AlgaeBase | title = AlgaeBase Website}}</ref> and harmful algae.<ref name="Observations on Alexandrium tamaren"/>

=== Long-term database in Bahía Blanca Estuary ===
Her contribution to the understanding of the occurrence of the winter-early spring diatom bloom in Bahía Blanca temperate estuary over the years 1978-1994<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=AM |title=Seasonal Succession Patterns of Phytoplankton in the Bahía Blanca Estuary (Argentina) |journal=Botanica Marina |date=1999 |volume=42 |issue=4 |pages=367–75 |doi=10.1515/BOT.1999.042|s2cid=85904295 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=AM |title=Long-term phytoplankton studies in the Bahía Blanca estuary, Argentina |journal=ICES Journal of Marine Science |date=1998 |volume=55 |issue=4 |page=665-60 |doi=10.1006/jmsc.1998.0375|doi-access=free }}</ref> represented the beginning of an invaluable long-term database of phytoplankton and in situ environmental variables. This dataset is one the most extensive (1978–present) in South America, which together with its high sampling frequency has allowed the detection of compositional and phenological shifts in the annual cycle of phytoplankton biomass and other components of the plankton.<ref name="AL2017">{{cite journal |last1=Abbate-Lopez |first1=C |last2=Marcovecchio |first2=J |title=Time-varying environmental control of phytoplankton in a changing estuarine system |journal=Science of the Total Environment |date=2017 |volume=609 |pages=1390–1400 |doi=10.1016/j.scitotenv.2017.08.002|pmid=28797145 |bibcode=2017ScTEn.609.1390L |hdl=11336/65979 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref name="G2012">{{cite journal |last1=Guinder |first1=VA |title=Dominance of the planktonic diatom Thalassiosira minima in recent summers in the Bahía Blanca Estuary, Argentina |journal=Journal of Plankton Research |date=2012 |volume=34 |issue=11 |pages=995–1000 |doi=10.1093/plankt/fbs060|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="G2010">{{cite journal |last1=Guinder |first1=V A |title=Long-term changes in phytoplankton phenology and community structure in the Bahía Blanca Estuary, Argentina |journal=Marine Biology |date=2010 |volume=157 |issue=12 |pages=2703–16 |doi=10.1007/s00227-010-1530-5|s2cid=21484704 }}</ref>

=== First report of E. huxleyi in Argentine Sea ===
In 1989, she participated in an oceanographic expedition in which she reported and described for the first time, the presence of high densities of the coccolithophore ''Emiliania huxleyi.''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gayoso |first1=AM |title=Bloom of Emiliania huxleyi (Prymnesiophyceae) in the western South Atlantic Ocean |journal=Journal of Plankton Research |date=1995 |volume=17 |issue=8 |pages=1717–22 |doi=10.1093/plankt/17.8.1717}}</ref>

== The Gayoso expedition ==
In [[Southern Hemisphere|austral]] summer 2021, a joint expedition took place along the [[Patagonian Shelf]] between Buenos Aires and Ushuaia to target the large ''Emiliania huxleyi'' annual bloom. The expedition was named after Gayoso to honor her scientific legacy.
*In November 2021, the [[RV Atlantis (1930)|Houssay]] schooner sailed from Ushuaia to Buenos Aires<ref>{{cite news |title=Un equipo del CONICET lidera la Campaña Oceanográfica Ana María Gayoso para estudiar el microbioma oceánico |url=https://bahiablanca.conicet.gov.ar/2021/11/17/un-equipo-del-conicet-lidera-la-campana-oceanografica-ana-maria-gayoso-para-estudiar-el-microbioma-oceanico/ |access-date=2021-11-17}}</ref>
*In December 2021, the [[Tara expedition|Tara Expedition]] schooner sailed in the opposite direction, from Buenos Aires to Ushuaia<ref>{{cite news |title=Looking for a coccolithophore bloom off Argentina by Flora Vincent |url=https://fondationtaraocean.org/en/mission-microbiomes/flora-vincent-coccolithophore-bloom-argentina/ |access-date=2025-01-07}}</ref>
